Test Case Title: Returns all documented fields for an existing booking
Preconditions: A booking created by the test (unique last name)
Test Data: Booking with firstname Jim, totalprice 111, dates 2018-01-01 to 2019-01-01
Expected Result: Status 200, content type JSON, and the body equals the created booking.

Test Steps: 1. Read the first id of GET /booking. 2. Send GET /booking/:id.
Expected Result: firstname and lastname are strings, totalprice is a number, depositpaid is a boolean, both dates look like YYYY-MM-DD.

Test Case Title: Accept: application/xml returns an XML body
Test Steps: 1. Send GET /booking/:id with the header Accept: application/xml.
Expected Result: Status 200. The body starts with the XML declaration and contains <booking> and <firstname>.

Test Case Title: A booking id that does not exist returns 404
The XML response is labelled with an XML content type
Test Steps: 1. Send GET /booking/:id with Accept: application/xml. 2. Read the Content-Type header.
Expected Result: The Content-Type contains "xml". Known defect D-03: the live API sends text/html.
Actual Result: Known defect: KNOWN DEFECT D-03: XML body is sent with Content-Type text/html (see DEFECTS.md)
